newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba silent on talk it could mediate Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Cuba silent on talk it could mediate Peru crisis.

text.p: The Cuban government declined to comment on Thursday on speculation it could help mediate an end to the crisis in Lima, where Marxist rebels are holding more than 100 hostages at the Japanese embassy residence.

There has been speculation in foreign media that the crisis could be resolved if President Fidel Castro's government allowed the rebels safe passage to Cuba. Cuban authorities have so far declined to comment on this possibility.
Asked again about a possible Cuban role, Foreign Ministry spokesman Miguel Alfonso told a regular weekly news briefing that "we have no comment in relation to this speculation."
He added that Cuba preferred prudence to rashness and this case was no exception. Alfonso added that diplomatic channels between Lima and Havana were "not just open but fluid." He did not elaborate.
Cuba last week refrained from condemning the attack on the Japanese residence by rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), and it has has still not done so.

The Cuban ambassador to Peru and another Cuban diplomat in Lima were among the original hostages taken by the rebels, who stormed the Japanese residence nine days ago during a cocktail reception. The two Cuban diplomats were among some 225 hostages released by the rebels on Sunday.
Cuban state-run media have reported on the crisis since it begun, but the reports have been brief and without commentary.

Last June, Castro helped secure the freedom of the kidnapped brother of former Colombian president Cesar Gaviria. Some of the leftist guerrillas and their families involved in that kidnapping were allowed to come to Cuba.
